title: KANTO >=1000 TEMPORARY-CLOSURE REOPEN AUDIT / PREFLIGHT 5
scope: Preflight/audit only. It combines the live Kanto >=1,000 inventory-unresearched pool with existing formal HOLDs whose recorded primary blocker was a temporary closure or temporary renovation only. No production venue, RaiBoC, hard case, source JSON, range, fingerprint, generated catalog/runtime, production total, or Tokyo Priority D record was reopened.

startSnapshot.preflight4AdoptQueue: closed: all three records reached production

policy.reason: The revised currentness policy must be applied without relaxing the independent numbered-seat, configuration, accessibility, and checksum gates.
policy.temporaryClosureRule: Temporary closure alone is not a blocker. Identity continuity, a current or issuer-maintained numbered chart, a coherent representative configuration, and no issuer-explicit seat-count/row/numbering change remain mandatory. Lack of a seating-change statement is recorded as an absence, never treated as proof.
policy.productionGate: ADOPT means only that a bounded implementation is likely feasible. It never authorizes transcription or promotion. Every ADOPT requires fresh independent human visual two-pass work, machine-expanded source equality, issuer subtotal reconciliation, an independent practical structural checksum, and a production stop on material mismatch. The 太田市民会館 correction is the standing mismatch rule: preserve the failed historical attempt and reread the chart; never alter ranges to fit a target.

excluded: tokyo-ota-aprico-main: the current 1,467 versus post-work 1,477 issuer-capacity conflict is an independent structure/currentness blocker, not temporary closure only.
kawaguchi-lilia-main: post-renovation complete numbered-chart evidence is independently missing.
tokyo-tiara-koto-main and every permanent-closure/replacement, SOURCE HOLD, NEED EVIDENCE, HARD-CASE, or RaiBoC record: not reopenable under a temporary-closure label.

candidatePool.productionExclusion: All 64 production ledger records, including the PREFLIGHT 4 implementations, were excluded before ranking.

method: Prioritised performance and ticket-lottery relevance, major urban use, current first-party numbered-chart quality, representative-configuration coherence, issuer subtotals, and practical independent verification; capacity alone did not rank a candidate.
Applied a yield penalty to event-dependent arena floors, generic movable-chair layouts, standing-first rooms, missing issuer domains, and any explicit seating-structure change.
Read historical reports only for the selected candidates immediately before fresh first-party checks; their old closure decisions remain historical facts rather than evidence of current layout.

rankedResearchOrder.reason: Nationally significant opera/orchestra hall; issuer maintains a five-floor chart, floor subtotals, wheelchair count, and a temporary-closure notice.
High-use Shinjuku performance hall; issuer now explicitly publishes the post-renovation 1,601-seat configuration, current seat-chart surface, pit condition, and accessibility semantics.
Active metropolitan concert/theatre hall with a detailed issuer seat PDF and unusually explicit fixed, floor, pit, wheelchair, and companion-seat semantics.
Temporary HVAC closure only; the city maintains a current normal-layout numbered PDF and complete fixed/movable/wheelchair checksum.
The highest remaining fixed-hall prospect from PREFLIGHT 4, but its recorded issuer hostname failed fresh DNS resolution and cannot supply current first-party seat evidence.
Active ticketed one-slope hall with issuer PDF, explicit fixed/standing/accessibility subtotals, a bounded pit condition, and a practical checksum path.

researched.identity: 東京文化会館〔大ホール〕 / 東京都台東区 / hall
firstPartyEvidence: https://www.t-bunka.jp/info/32755/ — issuer notice: temporary all-facility renovation closure from 2026-05-07 through FY2028 (planned), with no permanent closure, demolition, replacement, or seating-change statement.

https://www.t-bunka.jp/hall/large.html — issuer-maintained complete seating surface: 1F 1,282, 2F 238, 3F 355, 4F 268, 5F 160, total 2,303, plus 14 wheelchair spaces; printable chart link remains published while closed.
researched.currentnessAndClosure: TEMPORARY-RENOVATION PASS under the revised rule. The building is closed, but facility-space identity remains; no published seating, row, or numbering change was found. This absence is not proof of no later change, so implementation must re-fetch immediately before transcription and recheck after reopening.
researched.configuration: The issuer page describes a permanent five-floor numbered hall. No event-dependent floor, standing, or alternate numbered configuration was selected.
researched.accessibilityAndChecksum: Issuer gives 2,303 numbered seats plus 14 wheelchair spaces = 2,317, matching the inventory total. The chart must determine whether the wheelchair positions carry draw IDs; no relationship is inferred.
researched.chartAndFeasibility: Current issuer-maintained chart surface and printable chart are sufficient for a DENSE/JUDGMENT implementation prospect. Fresh visual inspection must establish every printed identifier and five-floor boundary; independent PDF/text-or-geometry and raster structural paths are practical but must not consume the human ranges.
researched.implementationVerificationPlan: Immediately before transcription, freshly re-fetch and record the issuer-maintained pre-renovation chart as the current implementation layout. If that re-fetch introduces no issuer-explicit seat-count, row-structure, or numbering change, complete fresh two-pass human extraction in different floor/traversal order; expand and compare both frozen sets against source bidirectionally; reconcile all five issuer floor subtotals and 2,303+14=2,317; and independently count practical chart structure. If all normal gates pass, production promotion may proceed before reopening; lack of a seating-change statement remains an absence, not proof. Any mismatch stops production and returns to the chart. Revalidate the chart and currentness after reopening.

researched.identity: 新宿区立新宿文化センター〔大ホール〕 / 東京都新宿区 / hall
firstPartyEvidence: https://www.regasu-shinjuku.or.jp/bunka-center/facilities/ — issuer states the 2023–2025 renovation widened seats and changed the hall from the historical 1,802 to a current 1,601 fixed seats.

https://www.regasu-shinjuku.or.jp/bunka-center/facilities/main-hall/ — current hall page has a seat-chart surface and states 1F 1,029 + 2F 572 = 1,601, pit use 1,479 (122 unavailable), and approximately 30 wheelchair spaces; it lists current booking and December 2026 performance use.
researched.currentnessAndClosure: PASS: the previous recheck gate is overtaken by the issuer's current post-renovation page. The old 1,802 inventory value is historical only and is not a transcription target.
researched.configuration: Select only the normal 1,601 fixed-seat chart prospect. The orchestra-pit condition is a separately described unavailable-seat mode and must not be manufactured by subtraction.
researched.accessibilityAndChecksum: Issuer floor checksum is 1,029+572=1,601. Wheelchair capacity is approximate (30), so the chart/issuer must establish whether positions are numbered, converted, or unnumbered before any source authoring.
researched.chartAndFeasibility: The live issuer-linked seat chart must be transcribed anew; its paired floor subtotal makes independent machine/human reconciliation practical.
researched.implementationVerificationPlan: Freeze two independent visual passes of the post-renovation chart; compare expanded source equality in both directions; reconcile 1F/2F totals and pit exclusion without arithmetic construction; independently validate chart cell/identifier structure; stop on every material mismatch.

researched.identity: めぐろパーシモンホール〔大ホール〕 / 東京都目黒区 / hall
firstPartyEvidence: https://www.persimmon.or.jp/about/hall_l.html and https://www.persimmon.or.jp/media/hall_l_seat.pdf — current issuer seat map and hall page: 1,200 capacity / 1,186 fixed, 1F 658 (512 with pit), 2F 429, balcony 92, 14 wheelchair spaces, 7 companion seats, and the exact companion seat numbers in 1F row 13.

https://www.persimmon.or.jp/lot.html — issuer closure notice: main hall unavailable 2027-01-12 through 2028-01-07 for ceiling non-structural-member fall-prevention work; unlike the small hall notice, it does not announce chair-back, count, row, or numbering work.
researched.currentnessAndClosure: TEMPORARY-RENOVATION PASS. The hall is actively programmed before the closure. The named work does not state a seating change; that is an absence, not a preservation guarantee, and creates a recheck obligation after the announced reopening.
researched.configuration: Fixed representative configuration only. Pit use is issuer-described separately; no alternate set is inferred.
researched.accessibilityAndChecksum: 1,186 fixed = 658 first floor + 429 second floor + 92 balcony + 7 numbered companion seats. Fourteen wheelchair spaces and the precise row-13 relation must be visually classified, never inferred from the total.
researched.chartAndFeasibility: One-page current issuer PDF with named floor/row blocks and explicit semantics is a high-yield ordinary two-pass candidate; independent PDF/raster structural checks are practical.
researched.implementationVerificationPlan: Two fresh independent human passes, source-to-pass set equality, issuer-floor/fixed/companion reconciliation, and an independent machine structural checksum. Before production, re-fetch the chart; after the announced closure, revalidate it against the reopened issuer material. Any change or mismatch stops promotion.

researched.identity: FOSTERホール（昭島市民会館）〔大ホール〕 / 東京都昭島市 / hall
firstPartyEvidence: https://www.city.akishima.lg.jp/shisei/shisetsu/1008430/1007674.html — city facility page: temporary closure through 2026-12-01 for renovation; 1,139-seat cultural-performance hall.

https://www.city.akishima.lg.jp/bunka/shogaigakushu/1007496/1002968/1007722/1007723.html and https://www.city.akishima.lg.jp/_res/projects/default_project/_page_/001/007/723/hall_zaseki_nomal.pdf — current city normal-layout chart: 1,031 fixed + 102 movable + 6 wheelchair = 1,139, with individually printed row/seat identifiers and a labelled wheelchair space.
researched.currentnessAndClosure: TEMPORARY-RENOVATION PASS. The city names HVAC/equipment renovation and a reopening date, not permanent closure, replacement, or an explicit seat-structure change. The missing change statement is not affirmative proof, so the reopening is a mandatory recheck event.
researched.configuration: One issuer-labelled normal layout; fixed and movable seats are separately itemised. No alternate configuration is inferred.
researched.accessibilityAndChecksum: Exact issuer checksum 1,031+102+6=1,139. The chart visibly labels wheelchair space and an explicit missing-number note; implementation must preserve both chart facts rather than filling gaps.
researched.chartAndFeasibility: The current official one-page PDF exposes individual labels and stable legend categories; ordinary independent visual two-pass plus PDF-text/raster-cell structure verification is practical.
researched.implementationVerificationPlan: Immediately before transcription, freshly re-fetch and record the issuer-maintained normal-layout chart. If that re-fetch introduces no issuer-explicit seat-count, row-structure, or numbering change, complete independent two-pass transcription, machine-expanded set equality, 1,031/102/6 issuer reconciliation, and an independent structural checksum. If all normal gates pass, production promotion may proceed before the 2026-12-01 reopening; lack of a seating-change statement remains an absence, not proof. Any changed asset, changed count/row/numbering, or mismatch stops production. Revalidate the chart and currentness at or after reopening.
